CQ headlights: vertex-only versus mixed

Original 1280 × 720 night renders, with identical cameras, lamp positions, beam strength and range. Vertex-only samples every supported receiver at vertices. Mixed retains vertex sampling on terrain and evaluates other supported receivers per pixel. Images have no exposure enhancement.

Measured on Intel N95 integrated graphics, Godot 4.7.2 Forward+, V-sync off. Each entry combines two 120-frame samples with reversed mode order; scene residency/LOD is frozen. Renderer CPU time is roughly unchanged. The 8-cone stress uses the exact same driver geometry and adds three lamp pairs without extra vehicle meshes.

UT99 avatar shader optimisation

Separate isolated 32-soldier render test. The optimized shader moves baked irradiance to vertices and retains per-pixel headlights. Maximum image difference: one 8-bit colour step. Frozen poses, same geometry and skin; these timings cannot be added to the full-map measurements.

The player views contain a frozen-pose UT99 Malcolm soldier. The render probe excludes shadows, normal-dependent headlight shading, network/controller work and populated gameplay simulation. GPU timing cannot be transferred to an unspecified GPU paired with an i7-12700. Raw samples and p95 results accompany this file.
